keyframe_review.note: 106,383 km2 with a bbox reaching 3.6 E (Champagne) and 50.5 N (Koblenz). The Alemanni page: 'The kingdom of Alamannia between Strasbourg and Augsburg lasted until 496'; the Alamannia page puts the Alemannic core on Lake Constance, the High Rhine, the Black Forest and the Upper Danube to the Lech. About 163 of the 475 cells lie in Lorraine, Champagne and the Trier district, which no page gives to the Alemanni. Neither page gives an area, so the infobox comparison is impossible. The northern limit at the Lahn is not contradicted: the Alemanni page puts Bad Ems 'on the northwestern edge of Alemannic settlement' (660-690).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 496-723, a period Cliopatria lacks (its Alamannia row has no shape for 500-723 and the Salian shape of 500 absorbs the whole Alamannia shape). The Tolbiac page: 'the northern half of the Alammanian lands went to the Franks' while 'the southern half sought protection under Theoderic'; the Alemanni page: 'put themselves under the protection of Theodoric the Great', and 'subjugated by the Franks under Theudebert I in 536'; the Alamannia page: after Dagobert I died in 638 'Alamannia broke from its Frankish rulers and largely stayed independent until the early 8th century'. The southern half is drawn as the Cliopatria 724 shape (Swabia round Lake Constance, 60,973 km2), the only dated Alamannic core in the data; the land under a protector or an overlord is the suzerain's tint (ostrogothic-kingdom vassal_start 500 to 536, then the Franks), not a loss of this dossier. Alsace is not drawn: the Alamannia page says 'Alsace and Raetia were outside Alamannia's scope in the early period' (the duchy of Alsace in the 630s).

60,973 km2, Swabia and north-east Switzerland, 7.3-11.1 E, 46.9-50.5 N. Lantfrid 'usurped the right to issue a law-code' between 724 and 730 (Lantfrid page), the duchy at its most independent; the shape is Swabia, not the whole 7th-century Alamannia of Alsace and Raetia Curiensis, which the Alamannia page puts outside. Cliopatria ends it in 731; the duchy lasted to 746 (Cannstatt page), covered by the next keyframe.

ledger.note: 462: the Kingdom of Alamannia appears between Strasbourg and Augsburg. 'The kingdom of Alamannia between Strasbourg and Augsburg lasted until 496' (Alemanni page); the year is Cliopatria's row start and the pages date no founding, so the confidence is 1. The Alemanni 'were ruled by independent tribal kings' (Alamannia page); Gibuld, 'the last known king', raided Passau about 470.

region.text: the northern half of the Alamannian lands, the Main, Neckar and Rhine-Main country, the Cliopatria 490 shape without the Lake Constance core

ledger.note: 496: Clovis beats the Alemanni at Tolbiac and the Franks take the northern half. 'the northern half of the Alammanian lands went to the Franks'; 'the southern half sought protection under Theoderic'. The page gives 496 as the traditional date and 506 for the revised chronology; the Alemanni page has 496 and 'conquered by Clovis I at the Battle of Tolbiac'. The region is the Cliopatria shape minus the 724 core (the researcher's reading of 'northern half'); the Salian Franks dossier takes the whole Cliopatria 499 shape instead.

536: the Franks under Theudebert I subjugate the Alemanni again and the kingdom becomes a nominal Frankish duchy. 'The Alemanni were again subjugated by the Franks under Theudebert I in 536' (Alemanni page); 'Alamannia became a nominal dukedom within Francia' (Alamannia page). The Kingdom of Alamannia continues as the Duchy of Alamannia: same land, same colour, the Frankish suzerainty is the Franks' tint to draw.

region.text: the duchy of Alamannia, Swabia round Lake Constance, passing to the Frankish rulers after the Cannstatt council

ledger.note: 746: Carloman's blood court at Cannstatt ends the duchy. 'in 746 ... an invitation by the Mayor of the Palace of Austrasia, Carloman' ... 'ended the independence of the duchy of Alamannia', 'after which it was ruled by Frankish dukes'; the Alamannia page dates direct Carolingian rule to 746 (Pepin the Short 748-768) and says several thousand nobles were executed for treason.

wars.name: Battle of Tolbiac

zones.text: the northern half of the Alamannian lands

wars.outcome: Frankish victory: 'The Franks were successful at Tolbiac and established their dominance over the Alamanni'; the northern half went to the Franks, the southern half to Theoderic's protection.
wars.note: 496 traditionally, 506 in the revised chronology the page cites; the site is usually given as Zulpich. The Alemanni king was killed ('as their leader had been killed with an axe'). Theoderic interceded with Clovis for the Alemanni.

wars.name: Frankish subjugation of Alamannia
wars.outcome: The Alemanni were 'again subjugated by the Franks under Theudebert I in 536'; Alamannia became a nominal dukedom within Francia. No territory changed hands in the data.
wars.note: The Alamannia page names Butilin and Haming as rulers 539-554 and says Alemannic auxiliaries 'most often fought in Italian campaigns'. The Alemanni page has a combined Frankish and Alemannic force beaten by Narses in 554.

wars.name: Frankish campaigns against the duchy of Alamannia
wars.outcome: The Arnulfing mayors of the palace reduced Alamannia to a Frankish province: Pepin of Herstal against Lantfrid 709-712, Charles Martel 722 and 730, Pepin the Short and Carloman 743, the Cannstatt blood court 746.
wars.note: Lantfrid page: Pepin of Herstal invaded in 709 and fought Duke Willehari, 'whose territory was limited to the Ortenau'; 'In 722 Charles Martel forcefully subdued the duchies of Alamannia and Bavaria'; 'In 730 Charles Martell invaded the duchy with an army once again', and Lantfrid died that year. The pages give no territorial change before 746, so no zone is drawn.

certainty.note: A tribal kingdom 'between Strasbourg and Augsburg' with no recorded frontier; the western and northern limits are approximate.

The Lech to the east and Lake Constance at the centre are the only features the Alamannia page gives; Alsace, Raetia and the Swiss Plateau are ill-defined, and the Cliopatria data has no shape for 500-723, so the keyframe is a reading.

notes: Cliopatria rows: Kingdom of Alamannia 462-499 (four shapes) and 724-731 (one shape), nothing for 500-723; this dossier keeps one state 462-746 and adds a keyframe 496-723 and one for 732-745. The 462-490 shapes are adjusted (Lorraine, Champagne and the Trier district removed); the Salian Franks note (eu-07-a) also found the shape reaching Lorraine. Capitals: none. The Alamannia page names Augsburg and Cannstatt only 'as capitals of individual counties'; the Alemanni page gives no seat. capitals is therefore empty. Status after 496 (for the other dossiers to draw): the southern half was under Theodoric's protection from Tolbiac to 536 (ostrogothic-kingdom carries vassal_start 500 and vassal_end 536 for it; the Ostrogoths dossier covering 493-499 should carry the 496 start); the Franks held it as a nominal duchy from 536 (Alemanni page) and 'broke from its Frankish rulers' after Dagobert I died in 638 (Alamannia page), staying 'largely independent until the early 8th century'; kingdom-of-the-franks should carry a vassal tint 536-638 and from 709. No event of this dossier changes the land in those years. Disagreement: the Alemanni page has Alsace conquered in 406 (so Alsace was Alemannic) while the Alamannia page says 'Alsace and Raetia were outside Alamannia's scope in the early period'; the 462-495 shapes keep Alsace, the later keyframes do not. Not covered: the Swiss Plateau (the Alemanni page names it for 406) has no gazetteer name; Raetia Curiensis ('absorbed in the early 10th century') is outside this dossier's years. The Alamannia page gives no area and no capital; the Lantfrid page does not mention Alsace or the Lech. Page budget: five of five (Alamannia, Alemanni, Battle of Tolbiac, Blood court at Cannstatt, Lantfrid; one URL_NOT_FOUND on 'Lantfrid, Duke of Alemannia').
